issues.description: Extract a named predicate for the layer-statement check instead of an inline negated conjunction.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged that `!(nodeName === 'layer' && typeof node.nodes === 'undefined')` is a double-negative buried in a dense boolean chain. A named helper like `isLayerStatement(node)` or `hasLayerBlock(node)` would make the CSS-spec invariant (statement form allowed, block form not) obvious at the call site.

issues.description: Replace `typeof node.nodes === 'undefined'` with a direct check matching PostCSS idioms.
issues.detail: The `typeof ... === 'undefined'` idiom conflates 'no block' with an undeclared identifier check and doesn't match surrounding PostCSS code. A direct `node.nodes === undefined` (or `Array.isArray`) names the AST fact — statement form vs block form — more plainly and matches the file's existing style.

issues.description: Add a symmetric accept-case test for `@layer foo;` (statement form) before `@import`.
issues.detail: The new test covers only the reject case (`@layer foo {}` before `@import`). The complementary accept case — bare `@layer foo;` before `@import` remaining valid — pins down both halves of the distinction this patch introduces and guards against a future refactor flipping the predicate. Three-line fixture, high value.

synthesis.summary: Unanimous accept-after-trivial-fixup. The fix is correct, minimal, and spec-aligned: it distinguishes the statement form of `@layer` (allowed before `@import`) from the block form (not allowed), and adds a regression test for the bug. All three reviewers converged on the same P2 polish items: extract a named predicate, prefer a direct `=== undefined` check over `typeof`, and add the symmetric accept-case test for `@layer foo;` before `@import`. No correctness or P0/P1 concerns raised.
